headline: Ten-year hit 5.365%. Minutes point to another hike.
standfirst: Wednesday took back a little of Tuesday's records. The S&P 500 fell 0.22% to 7,801.77, the Dow 0.66% to 51,179.87 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.22% to 27,538.69, ending four- and five-day winning streaks, while the Russell 2000 fell 1.31% and industrials were the weakest sector, down 2.18%. The ten-year yield touched 5.365%, its highest since 2002, before a $39 billion auction cleared at 5.300% with firm demand, and it closed near 5.28%. The minutes of the September meeting showed all 19 participants backed the hike and most expect another by year-end, with no date; October is priced as a hold at about 83%. European stocks lost about 1%, with Italy down 2.5% as French bonds sold off again, gold touched a two-month low and Bitcoin fell. This morning Asia is lower, the Kospi down 1.4% and Singapore 3.1%, and Brent is $102.61, up 2.4%, on reports that Washington is weighing renewed strikes on Iran, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a Gulf storm. Today: claims, the thirty-year auction at 13:00 ET, Musalem, and Waller on the calendar.

bullets.title: Rates: the ten-year touched 5.365%, the auction cleared at 5.300%, and the minutes point to another hike
bullets.text: The ten-year yield touched 5.365%, the highest since 2002, and the thirty-year about 5.73% during Wednesday's session, then eased after $39 billion of ten-year notes cleared at 5.300% with a bid-to-cover of 2.77 against 2.71 last time and a 2.52 average, and indirect bidders taking about 80% of the notes. The ten-year closed near 5.28%, up about 1bp, the thirty-year near 5.67% and the two-year near 4.77%. The long Treasury fund fell 0.17% and is down 6.15% over a month. The minutes of the 16 September meeting showed all 19 participants supported the hike and that most judged another increase likely appropriate by year-end, though they stressed they approach each meeting with an open mind; many called a higher path prudent insurance against persistent inflation, and inflation risks were seen as tilted up on energy prices and AI-related investment. Futures price the 28 October meeting as a hold at about 83%, with about three more quarter-point hikes priced by June, according to Morningstar. The New York Fed's survey showed one-year inflation expectations at their highest in more than three years. Today brings $22 billion of thirty-year bonds at 13:00 ET, against 5.308% last month.

bullets.title: Equities: a small fall in the indexes, led by industrials, chips and small caps, and health care up
bullets.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.22% to 7,801.77, a day after its record, the Dow 0.66% to 51,179.87 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.22% to 27,538.69; the Russell 2000 fell 1.31% to 2,793.20 and the VIX closed at 15.08. Health care rose 1.03% and was the only sector fund higher, while industrials fell 2.18%, materials 1.51% and real estate 1.29%; technology slipped 0.30% but is still up 7.20% over a month. Chip stocks led the weakness, with Microchip and NXP down more than 3% and Analog Devices, Arm, Qualcomm and Texas Instruments more than 2%, and crypto-linked shares such as Strategy fell more than 5% as Bitcoin dropped; the broker-dealer index fell 2.6%. SpaceX was reported to be seeking about $40 billion of financing to buy Nvidia chips. PepsiCo reports before the open today and Delta tomorrow; the banks begin on 13 October. Futures were mixed overnight.

bullets.title: Oil: Brent $102.61 on reports of renewed US strikes on Iran, Houthi attacks and a Gulf storm
bullets.text: December Brent is $102.61, up 2.41%, and WTI $90.20, up 2.17%, after both settled lower on Wednesday, Brent at $100.20 and WTI at $88.28, when the International Energy Agency agreed to speed the release of stocks and prioritise diesel. Overnight NBC reported that President Trump and his national security team have discussed restarting large-scale US military operations in Iran in the coming weeks, and The Atlantic reported that the Pentagon was asked for strike options before the November midterms. The Houthis' recent attacks on Saudi airports, Iran's attacks on tankers near Hormuz, and a tropical storm forecast to become a hurricane and reach the northern Gulf coast by the weekend add to it, against a surprise draw in US crude inventories and shipping through Hormuz briefly at pre-war highs. Heating oil is $4.71, up 1.14%, and natural gas is up 7.15% on the week. Brent's 1M column still straddles the 30 September roll to December.

bullets.title: Europe and Asia: Italy down 2.5% and French bonds sold off again; Asia lower, Singapore down 3.1%
bullets.text: European stocks closed sharply lower: the Stoxx 600 fell about 1.1%, the DAX 1.4% to 25,091, the CAC 40 1.22% to 7,769.21, the FTSE 100 0.79% to 10,458.50, Italy's FTSE MIB 2.51% and Spain's Ibex 1.8%, with banks down about 3.4% as French ten-year yields touched 4.92% and protests and the IMF's call for fiscal tightening revived Tuesday's worries. The euro fell 0.63% to about $1.119 and is $1.12 this morning; German industrial production rose 2.0% in August, ahead of expectations. Futures point to a flat open in London and Frankfurt and a small gain in Paris. In Asia the Nikkei is down 0.84% near 69,446, the Kospi down 1.42% near 6,707 despite Samsung Electronics guiding to a record third-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, Hong Kong down 0.69%, Taiwan 0.84% and Singapore 3.13%; Shanghai reopened after a week closed and is down 0.27%. South Korea is shut on Friday for a holiday. The ECB's accounts of its 10 September hike are out at 07:30 ET.

bullets.title: Gold, crypto and the Americas: gold touched $4,066, Bitcoin is $82,834, and Canada fell 2.1%
bullets.text: Spot gold fell about 1.2% to near $4,114 on Wednesday, touching $4,066, a two-month low, with the minutes and higher yields cited; futures settled at $4,140.70 and are $4,155.70 this morning, up 0.36%, but still down 6.38% over a month. Silver is $60.12, platinum up 1.66% and copper up 1.04%. Bitcoin fell more than 2% on Wednesday and is $82,834, with Ether down 4.41% and Litecoin down 8.28% on the week. The Canada ETF fell 2.10% and the TSX 1.70%, the Brazil ETF 1.47% and the Bovespa 0.74% to 204,302, and the Chile ETF 2.30%; the Brazil ETF is still up 10.95% on the week after last Monday's election-driven surge. The dollar moved little: the yen is 158.27, the euro $1.12, and India's rupee 96.74 after the central bank's hike to 5.5% on Wednesday. Coffee fell 3.86% and cocoa 2.07% this morning; sugar is up 15.08% over a month.

calendar.note: The calendar has Waller early Thursday; a Reuters note had placed him, Kashkari and Musalem on Wednesday, and no remarks from him were found overnight, so check the time before relying on it.

calendar.event: ECB accounts; claims 08:30 ET; PepsiCo 08:15 ET
calendar.note: The accounts of the 10 September hike land after euro-area inflation printed 3.8%, French ten-year yields neared 5% and the market cut its ECB path. Claims are seen at 200,000 after 197,000.
The last of the week's three auctions. The long bond touched 5.73% on Wednesday and closed near 5.67%; the last auction cleared at 5.308%, and the ten-year drew firm demand at 5.300%.
Seen 6.5% after 6.4%. The Bank of Canada is at 2.25% with its decision, policy report and press conference on 28 October; oil pass-through argues for a hike and a rising jobless rate against.
Seen 47.6 after 48.1; one-year inflation expectations were 4.6% and five-year 3.4%. Delta reports before the open.

calendar.event: Columbus Day: US bond market closed; Hammack 12:50 ET
calendar.note: Equities trade; Treasuries and the banks do not. The IMF and World Bank meetings run in Washington through the week.
The first CPI after the September hike: August was 3.4% on the year with the monthly at +0.4%, and core +0.3% on the month. Fourteen days before the 28 October decision.
Retail sales rose 1.2% in August with the control group at +1.4%; core PPI was 4.6% on the year. Claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey print the same morning.

sessionNote: Thursday opens with Asia and Europe leaning lower after a Wednesday in which yields touched their highest since 2002 and then came back, and with oil up 2% on reports that Washington is weighing renewed strikes on Iran. The week's three Treasury auctions end today at 13:00 ET with $22 billion of thirty-year bonds, after a three-year at the highest yield since 2006 with below-average indirect demand and a ten-year at 5.300% with strong demand. The minutes gave no date for the next hike, so the 28 October meeting rests on CPI on 14 October; futures price October as a hold at about 83% and December as the likelier move. Brent is $102.61, the euro $1.12 and gold near $4,155 after Wednesday's two-month low. Korea is shut tomorrow and the Kospi is down 1.4%; mainland China has reopened after a week. A day to read the long-bond auction and claims, and to treat the Iran headlines as unconfirmed reports.
watchOut: Reading the ten-year's retreat from 5.365% as relief. It closed up 1bp at about 5.28% after an auction at 5.300% that had firm indirect demand, and the minutes say most officials expect another hike; the thirty-year auction at 13:00 ET is the longest-maturity test and the yield can reopen. Second, the Iran headlines: NBC and The Atlantic reported discussion of renewed strikes citing sources, and no decision has been announced; Brent has moved 2% on the reports and can reverse as quickly. Third, the map's Brent 1M column, which still straddles the 30 September roll and shows a gain next to WTI's fall. Fourth, thin Asia and a US-heavy day: South Korea is shut on Friday and Singapore's 3.1% fall has no stated cause in the reports found. Fifth, the Waller time on the calendar is unconfirmed. Size for the 13:00 ET auction, not for the index.

The August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion on record imports, euro-area retail sales rose 0.8% against 1.0% expected, India's central bank raised its rate to 5.5% and the Kospi fell about 1.5%. Brent was $101.45 on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker incidents near Hormuz.

archive.headline: Nasdaq record. Ten-year at a 24-year high.
archive.summary: Brazil's Ibovespa jumped 7.7% to a record after Flavio Bolsonaro led the presidential first round, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on Nvidia and the S&P 500 at 7,773.95. ISM services prices paid rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, and the ten-year touched 5.349%, its highest since 2002, before closing near 5.31%. Brent fell about 2% to $100.3 on a G7 stock release, and the euro touched a 17-month low near $1.116 on French and Spanish politics.

archive.headline: Payrolls 29,000. Yields rose anyway.
archive.summary: September payrolls rose 29,000 against about 90,000 expected with a net 60,000 downward revision, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.1%; October's Fed hike went to about 22% priced and the Nasdaq touched a record, but the ten-year closed about 3bp higher after Logan said half a point more is needed. The G7 agreed a 100 million barrel stock release, euro-area inflation printed 3.8%, Tokyo core CPI 2.7% and the dollar index reached a 17-month high.

archive.headline: Payrolls 29,000. Yields rose anyway.
archive.summary: Weekend edition. October's Fed hike went from more than 70% priced on Monday to about 25% by Thursday on Williams, a 3.0% core PCE and Jefferson, while the long end set 2002 highs on a 2.2% GDP revision, a 58.8 Chicago PMI and ISM prices paid at 77.9; the ten-year touched 5.344% and closed 5.233%. Brent rose 4.4% on China's fuel-export halt and a third US carrier group, Nike cut its guidance, the euro hit a 16-month low on France's budget and Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7%.

archive.headline: Core PCE 3.0%. Bonds' worst month since 2022.
archive.summary: Core PCE printed 3.0% against 3.3% after the BEA's annual revision rewrote July, ADP beat at 90,000, final Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% and Chicago PMI jumped to 58.8; October's hike odds slid to 35–40% while the ten-year and thirty-year rose again to close a September in which the ten-year added about 50bp, its worst month since 2022. Micron beat and guided above consensus; the November Brent contract expired at $103.53; the Nikkei rose 3.24%.
